rows.title: Commodity page and Commodity details wording, the Species column, the 'Select a commodity' error, the soft Save and return, and the error order match Design Release 2.1
rows.detail: The two live-animals commodity pages keep today's frame, today's server-side search behind its Search button and today's catalogue, and change what they say and how they save to Design Release 2.1's. The commodity page gets the ITAHC inset text, the live-animals search hint (common name, code or Latin name, with no 3-character sentence) and the Trade Tariff link's '(opens in a new tab)' on its own line. Its 'Select a commodity' error always sits on the search field, whether or not results are listed; 'Save and return to overview' saves the selection as it stands without checking it; and a selection made only of 01061900 species clears the unweaned animals answer, because that question is not asked for them. Commodity details gets the caption 'Description of the goods', a Species column in the Selected commodities table listing the Latin names chosen under each commodity, and an error summary that lists its errors by question, every number of animals error before any number of packages error. Every changed or added English string gets its Welsh counterpart, marked as a machine draft, so the Welsh pages do not fall behind.
acceptanceCriteria: The commodity page's inset text reads 'You must submit a separate notification for every single ITAHC. You must also submit a notification for goods that do not need an ITAHC.' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-073; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-005; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p1-043; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-011)

On a live-animals notification the commodity search hint reads 'You can search by common name (for example, cattle), commodity code (0102), or Latin name (Bos taurus).', with no 'Enter at least 3 characters.' sentence. rows.title: Commodity pages chain as journey steps around the main import reason
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 makes the two commodity pages steps of the journey rather than an overview task that returns to the overview. The commodity page's back link goes to origin and Save and continue goes on to the main import reason; Commodity details comes after the main import reason, its back link goes to the commodity page, and Save and continue goes on to identification, additional or arrival details, whichever applies first. Opened from its overview task, each page still returns to the overview. The k6 performance suite's live-animals walk visits the main import reason between the two commodity pages in the same change, so the suite keeps running.
acceptanceCriteria: The commodity page's back link goes to the origin of the import page. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-074; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-018, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-026; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p1-048; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-011)

After a valid choice on the commodity page, Save and continue goes to the main import reason page; opened from the overview it returns to the overview instead, and opened from check answers it returns to check answers. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-100; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-052; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p1-066; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-196; c-015)

(prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-051; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p5-001; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p2-013, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p2-014)

The Commodity details page's back link goes to the commodity page ('What are you importing?'). (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-004, prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-005; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p5-009, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-055; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p2-024)

Reached in the journey from the main import reason page, a valid Save and continue on Commodity details goes to Identification details when any chosen species needs identifiers, otherwise to Additional details when that page applies, otherwise to the arrival details; opened from its overview task it returns to the overview. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-049; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p5-022, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-047; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p2-027; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-196)

Both pages still end with 'Save and continue', 'Save and return to overview' and 'Cancel and return to overview', and opening Commodity details with no commodity on the notification still sends the trader to the commodity page. The k6 performance suite's live-animals walk, run against the local stack, visits the main import reason page between the commodity page and Commodity details and passes every check it makes on each page. rows.gate: Walk the journey from origin to arrival details: this row moves Commodity details after the main import reason, and every row that walks the journey from here on rests on that order.
rows.notes: Unchanged in substance; ruling 2026-10-09 afternoon (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-011) confirms the commodity pages' place in the journey goes ahead on today's data. Combines the back-link slices (req-089, -108) with the next-step slices (req-087, -117, -118) and the k6 step-list slice (req-1761): the same journey flow change, observed only together, and the suite breaks the moment the order changes. c-015 (ruled): Design Release 2.1's chaining wins; opened from its overview task a page returns to the overview (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-196). c-016: both pages keep the three return controls. c-018: the no-commodity redirect stays. c-225 (ruled): the performance suite changes in each increment whose change breaks one of its k6 scripts, on that increment's branch name; its 'Cow' search changes with the blocked catalogue row (req-1919), not here. Where Commodity details goes after a change from check answers is req-119's, which the type-question-and-templates branch holds; this row does not change it. The main import reason page already exists; the reason-and-additional-details rows change its copy, not its place. Depends on inc-001 (journey-foundation), which reorders the opening run's step list in the shared flow; this row makes the pages' own back links and next steps agree. The tests repo's journey flow walks the new order.

rows.title: Live-animal commodity catalogue matches Design Release 2.1, once commodities come from MDM
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1's live-animal catalogue: 0102 named 'Cattle' with 11 species, Horse with Donkey and Mule, 'Domestic cat' and 'Domestic dog', Ferret and Other live mammals on 01061900, Ornamental fish in place of Fish, and the poultry, livestock, rabbit, camel, ostrich, parrot, reptile and bee commodities. DR2.1's misspelt horse names and its duplicated 'Other mammal' entry are corrected rather than copied, because the species text reaches the receiving service as the scientific name. The number of packages question follows the new list, and the k6 performance suite's commodity search moves from 'Cow' to a term the new catalogue matches. Ruling 2026-10-09 afternoon records this as work but blocks it until commodities come from MDM through trade-imports-reference-data, which serves no commodity list today; the area is re-distilled then, and the repos it builds in may change with that.
acceptanceCriteria: Searching finds Pig (0103), Sheep (010410), Goat (010420), Chicken (010511), Turkey (010512), Duck (010513), Goose (010514), Guinea fowl (010515), Rabbit (010614), Camel (010613), Ostrich (010633), Parrot (010632), Reptile (010620) and Bees (01064100), each with DR2.1's species. rows.title: Commodity search results sorted and bolded, and a selected panel of removable species chips, once commodities come from MDM
rows.detail: The server-rendered commodity page lists results alphabetically with the matched text in bold, and shows what has been chosen as one bold commodity line followed by a chip per species, by Latin name, each with its own remove button, so a trader can drop one choice without clearing everything. Ruling 2026-10-09 afternoon blocks these four until commodities come from MDM, then re-distils them. The rest of the old row (the error on the search field, the soft Save and return, clearing the unweaned answer) moved to the commodity wording row and goes ahead.
acceptanceCriteria: Search results list commodities alphabetically by commodity name, and the species under each alphabetically by their label ('common name (Latin name)', or 'commodity name (Latin name)' where a species has no common name). (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-084, prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-109; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-026)

The selected panel lists each chosen commodity as a bold 'Commodity (code):' line followed by one chip per chosen species showing its Latin name, such as 'Cattle (0102):' then 'Bos taurus'. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-035, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-041, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p13-023; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p1-056)

rows.title: Waiting on design: commodity search lists results as the trader types, once commodities come from MDM
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1's commodity search lists results as the trader types, behind an icon search button, announces results and selections in a polite live region, and keeps the typed text open for more ticks, with Escape closing the results. Ruling 2026-10-09 afternoon keeps today's server-side search, which already works without JavaScript, and puts this behaviour in the waiting-on-design theme as design question 3's increment; it is also blocked on commodities coming from MDM. When both have happened it is built as design says with an accepted component, or dropped if design drops it.
acceptanceCriteria: With JavaScript, typing in the commodity search lists matching results as the trader types, with no Search press, behind an icon search button whose visually hidden text is 'Search'. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-078, prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-081; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-008, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-023; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p1-053, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-008)
The page does not carry the whole commodity list: results come from the service's commodity catalogue as the trader types. (c-012)

Without JavaScript the page keeps the Search button, lists nothing for a query under 3 characters, and renders results and the selected panel on the server. (trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p8-059; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-059; c-012)

A visually hidden polite live region announces the number of results, such as '11 results available', and the number of species chosen, such as '1 option selected' and '2 options selected', and is left empty after Clear all; the results list is labelled 'Commodity search results'. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-029, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-030, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-032, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-038, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-042, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-046; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p1-054)

With JavaScript, ticking a species keeps the typed search text, leaves the results open for more ticks and adds the species to the selected panel. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-039, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-039-m1; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p1-057)

With JavaScript, pressing Escape closes the results and empties the search field, and the selection stays in the panel. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-044; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p1-057)
A species chosen as you type is saved by Save and continue like one chosen without JavaScript. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-039)
With and without JavaScript, the commodity page has no serious or critical axe violations under the wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and wcag22aa tags. (trace:animals-fit trace-animals-fit-p8-057)
Every new English string, such as the live region's announcements and the results label, has its Welsh counterpart, marked as a machine draft. (repo:frontend repo-frontend-p5-044)
rows.gate: Look at the as-you-type search with and without JavaScript, with a screen reader's announcements, before any other client-side component copies its pattern; check its script is in the built bundle on a fresh stack.
openQuestions: Design must answer design question 3 (commodity search as you type): build it as design says with an accepted component and no custom JavaScript copied from the prototype, or drop it if design drops it (ruling 2026-10-09 afternoon, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-059, -p2-008; c-012).

Blocked also until commodities come from MDM: whoever owns the MDM integration must make the MDM commodity list reach the animals frontend through trade-imports-reference-data, after which the area is re-distilled (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-060, -p2-008; c-278).
rows.notes: Combines the live-typing slice (req-072), the live-region slice (req-073) and the tick-and-Escape slice (req-074): one client-side behaviour on one page, none observable apart from the others. Belongs to the waiting-on-design theme, as design question 3's increment. Kept apart from the catalogue row because it carries a second blocker (design question 3) the catalogue does not. The existing row inc-014 also holds the germinal set's copy of this behaviour (req-1782, from the germinal-products area); the combiner should merge that area's draft into this row, as ruling 2026-10-09 afternoon makes design question 3 one increment. Depends on the search-results row (inc-013), whose sorting, bolding and chips the results reuse. The prototype's whole list shipped with the page is not copied (c-012 outcome; its overruled claims are not named). A new client-side entry must be wired into the frontend's build, or it fails silently.

rows.title: The live-animals commodity search no longer offers germinal products
rows.detail: Ruling 2026-10-09 makes germinal products a set of its own with its own catalogue, so the live-animals catalogue gives up the 12 germinal-product lines it holds today and a live-animals trader is never offered semen, embryos or ova. Splitting today's lines between the sets is set architecture, not list content, so it goes ahead on today's data rather than waiting on MDM.
acceptanceCriteria: On a live-animals notification, searching the commodity page for 'semen', 'embryos', 'ova' or the germinal codes 05111000 and 05119985 lists no results: the live-animals catalogue offers none of the 12 germinal-product lines it holds today. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-006, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-025, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-026; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-018, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-019; prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p2-109; c-222)

On a live-animals notification, today's live-animal commodities (Cow, Horse, Cat, Dog and Fish) are still found and can still be chosen and saved. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-019, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-025; repo:tests repo-tests-p1-042)
rows.notes: req-1754 already sits in inc-016 (the germinal commodity page offers today's 12 germinal lines, and the live-animals page no longer does), beside the germinal-products area's req-092, which states the same removal from the germinal side; ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-018 places it there. The combiner should fold this draft into inc-016 with the germinal-products area's draft for that row, not keep it as a row of its own. c-222 (ruled): each set's catalogue holds only its own commodities. The code it changes is the live-animals commodity service, which the commodities-and-reason theme owns, so it is listed as shared: the combiner must either give that one change to the germinal-products theme for this row or keep germinal-products depending on commodities-and-reason, as it does today. The tests repo's commodities spec lists today's catalogue and changes with it.

rows.title: Germinal Commodity details lists its errors by question
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 orders the Commodity details error summary by question. Ruling 2026-10-09 splits that rule per set: on the germinal-products set every total gross weight error comes before every number of packages error. V4 makes temperature optional, so it raises no error and never appears in the summary.
acceptanceCriteria: On a germinal-products notification, pressing Save and continue on Commodity details with errors on several species lists every Total gross weight error, species by species, before every Number of packages error, each linking to its own field. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-042; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-021, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-057; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-051)

On a germinal-products notification, Temperature never appears in the Commodity details error summary, and Commodity details with no temperature chosen, a blank total gross weight and a valid number of packages for every species shows no error and saves. (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-021, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-023; c-232)
rows.notes: req-1762 already sits in inc-177 (germinal Commodity details checks weight and packages, listing errors by question), with the germinal-products area's weight and packages validation requirements; the combiner should fold these two criteria into that row rather than keep a separate row. It is the germinal half of req-114, which the live-animals wording row (inc-011) builds. c-232 (ruled): the prototype's blank-weight and blank-temperature errors are not built, and its overruled claims are not named. Depends, as inc-177 does, on the germinal Commodity details questions row (inc-017), which puts the fields on the page.

rows.title: Germinal Commodity details task shows Complete on valid packages
rows.detail: The overview's task status tells the trader what is left to do. Ruling 2026-10-09 splits the Commodity details completeness rule per set: on the germinal-products set the task is Complete once every chosen species has a valid number of packages and any total gross weight entered is valid. V4 makes total gross weight and temperature optional, so neither holds the task back, and Design Release 2.1's bar of a weight above 0 and a temperature is not built.
acceptanceCriteria: On a germinal-products notification, the overview's Commodity details task shows Complete when every chosen species has a whole number of packages from 1 to 1,000, with total gross weight and temperature left blank. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-024, prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-054; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-021, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-023; c-232; c-234)

On a germinal-products notification, the overview's Commodity details task does not show Complete while any chosen species has no number of packages, or has a total gross weight entered that is not valid, such as 0. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-054; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-057; trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p12-053)
On a germinal-products notification with no species chosen, the overview's Commodity details task does not show Complete. (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p3-054)
rows.notes: req-1763 already sits in inc-099 (the germinal products Overview), because only that overview shows the task status; the combiner should keep it there, with these three criteria as that row's Commodity details Complete criteria, merged with the notification-hub area's draft for the row. It is the germinal half of req-126, whose live-animals half exists. c-232 (ruled): weight and temperature do not hold the task back. c-234 (ruled): packages are the line's quantity, at most 1,000 (the limit req-1789 sets in inc-177). Depends, as inc-099 does, on inc-017 and inc-177 for the stored fields and their validity.
